From the owner
Choosing the right bathroom remodeling contractor is one of the most important decisions you will make during your renovation. The quality of the contractor directly determines the quality of the finished result — and in bathroom remodeling, poor workmanship can lead to water damage, mold, and costly repairs down the road. Start by evaluating experience. How long has the contractor been doing bathroom work specifically? Bathroom remodeling — especially wet area construction like showers and tubs — requires specialized knowledge in waterproofing, tile installation, and plumbing. General experience in construction does not automatically translate to expertise in bathrooms. Ask about licensing and insurance. A professional bathroom remodeling contractor carries proper licensing and liability insurance. This protects you in case of accidents or damage during the project. Never hire a contractor who cannot provide proof of insurance. Request a written estimate. A detailed written estimate that breaks down materials, labor, and scope of work shows that the contractor has thought through your project carefully. Vague verbal quotes are a red flag. Ask who actually does the work. This is the question most homeowners forget to ask. Many companies use subcontractors — meaning the person who sold you the project is not the person who installs it. Find out if the owner is involved in the work, or if your project will be handed off to someone you have never met. Check references and review

From the owner
The kitchen has to handle more daily activity than almost any other room in the house. Cooking, food preparation, storage, cleaning, and family gatherings all compete for the same limited space. A skilled kitchen remodeler can help turn those competing needs into a more efficient layout. BetterMost Construction and Restoration considers practical details such as countertop workspace, cabinet storage, appliance placement, lighting, and traffic flow when approaching a kitchen project. One common mistake is choosing finishes before deciding how the kitchen should function. A beautiful countertop will not solve a layout where the refrigerator blocks a walkway or frequently used cookware is stored too far from the cooking area. Think about how the room is used at breakfast, during meal preparation, and when several people are moving through it at once. Those everyday patterns can reveal opportunities that a simple style makeover may miss. The best kitchen remodels are not necessarily the most elaborate. Sometimes moving one cabinet, improving lighting, or creating a better work triangle makes the biggest difference in how the room feels every day.

By reimagining these essential corners of your home, you invite clarity and ease into every morning. Take time to consider how your environment shapes your well-being. Roof Leaks and Damaged Shingles: When to Call for Repairs A small roof problem is easy to ignore until water finds its way inside. Knowing when a leak or damaged shingle needs attention can help you avoid larger repairs later. Some signs show up inside the home: brown or yellow stains on ceilings, peeling paint near the roofline, damp insulation in the attic, or a musty smell that doesn't go away. Outside, look for shingles that are cracked, curling, or missing, exposed nails, or granules collecting in gutters. Damaged flashing around chimneys, vents, and skylights is another common source of leaks. It's usually worth calling for repairs when a leak returns after drying out, when several shingles are damaged at once, or after a heavy storm. Waiting can let moisture soak into decking and insulation, which turns a simple repair into something more involved. It's also worth noting that where water appears inside isn't always directly below where it enters the roof, so a professional assessment helps trace the real source rather than patching the wrong spot. At GC&E Services, we handle roof repairs as part of our residential construction work in Sedona and nearby areas. With over 25 years of experience and a general contracting license (ROC #324490), we can assess the damage and explain your options. Contact our team about your roof repair. #RoofRepair #RoofLeak #GCEServices

Reface or Replace Your Kitchen Cabinets? Cabinets are often the biggest decision in a kitchen remodel. Refacing works well when the cabinet boxes are still solid and you mainly want a new look. Replacement makes more sense if you are changing the layout, need better storage, or the existing cabinets have water damage or structural wear. Countertops come next: quartz is engineered, non-porous and does not need sealing, while granite is a natural stone with unique veining that needs periodic sealing to resist staining. We help Connecticut homeowners weigh these choices during a free in-home consultation. Ask us about your kitchen remodel.

Should You Replace Kitchen Cabinets or Keep the Existing Ones? Kitchen cabinets can represent one of the largest decisions in a remodel, both visually and financially. If your existing cabinet boxes are structurally sound, the layout works well, and storage meets your needs, keeping or cosmetically updating them may allow you to invest elsewhere. Replacement makes more sense when cabinets are damaged, storage is inefficient, or you're changing the kitchen layout. Budget matters too. Custom Bath & Kitchen's Massachusetts remodeling guide notes that cabinetry frequently represents a major portion of the overall kitchen investment, and choosing between stock, semi-custom, and fully custom configurations can significantly affect cost. Kitchens in Jamison tend to share the same problem. A lot of the homes around Warwick Greene, Mountain View, and the Estates of Bucks County Country Club went up in the late '80s and '90s, back when builders walled the breakfast nook off from the family room. It made sense then. It makes very little sense now, and it's why so many of these kitchens feel smaller than the square footage says they are. The fix is usually the wall. Take it down and you get the sightline, the island, and the room everyone ends up standing in anyway. Gemini Home Remodeling handles kitchen remodels throughout Bucks County, with a dedicated project manager on your job and a written schedule showing which trades are in your home each day. Fall Is the Right Time to Check Your Home’s Exterior Before colder weather settles into North Jersey, take a good look at the parts of your home that work hardest through fall and winter — the roof, siding, windows, doors, and exterior finishes. Loose or aging siding, worn roofing, drafty windows, peeling paint, and weathered exterior surfaces can become bigger problems once temperatures drop and winter weather arrives. Addressing these issues now can help protect your home, improve comfort, and prevent avoidable repair costs later. H2M Renovation & Construction Group provides roofing, siding, windows and doors, exterior painting and staining, and power washing for homeowners across Paramus, Bergen County, Passaic County, Essex County, Hudson County, and surrounding North Jersey communities. HHI Builders starts by understanding how you use the home—primary residence, second home, or vacation property—and what is not working in the current layout. A request for a “bigger kitchen” may actually point to a poorly placed island, a wall that limits flow, or nearby square footage that is not being used well. Before construction, we document the existing home, develop layouts, coordinate cabinetry and selections, review architectural and engineering needs, and account for electrical, plumbing, permitting, and community requirements. A luxury bathroom is not about adding more—it’s about making the right design decisions. This bathroom remodeling project in **Edison, NJ** features a freestanding soaking tub paired with dramatic blue porcelain tile, matte black fixtures, and a built-in niche. The contrast creates a strong focal point while keeping the overall space clean and sophisticated. For homeowners planning a bathroom remodel, one important design principle is to choose **one feature that anchors the room**. It could be a freestanding tub, a custom shower, a statement vanity, or distinctive tile. The remaining finishes should complement that feature rather than compete with it. In this bathroom, the freestanding tub becomes the centerpiece while the surrounding tile adds depth, warmth, and character. From the owner
Small Bathroom Ideas for Norwalk, CT Homes If you live in East Norwalk, Rowayton, Silvermine, or West Norwalk, you probably know the “great house, tiny bath” combo. Good news: small doesn’t have to feel cramped. With the right plan, you can turn a tight space into a room that’s bright, practical, and easy to clean. Below are small bathroom ideas we’ve seen work again and again in Norwalk, tested against salt air, older framing, and real New England seasons. What Really Limits Space (and How to Fix It) Older homes bring charm and quirks. Doorways aren’t always square, vent runs can be long, and moisture loves to linger. So the best small bathroom ideas start with function: clearances, storage you’ll actually use, and a shower that doesn’t soak the whole room. Small Bathroom Ideas for Norwalk Homes: 7 Creative Renovations 1. Layout first, looks second Pretty tile won’t fix a clumsy layout. A few moves that pay off: Right-size the vanity. A 24–30″ vanity with drawers often beats a bulkier cabinet. Drawers = reachable storage. Pocket or out-swing door. Free those precious inches near the toilet or vanity. Wall-hung where you can. A floating vanity (and even a wall-hung toilet) opens floor space and makes mopping a two-minute job. Tip: Tape the footprint on the floor before you buy anything. The best small bathroom ideas are the ones that fit your exact room, not a showroom.

From the owner
Home remodeling in Frederick usually means coordinating several trades, and that coordination is where most of the stress in a renovation actually lives. A kitchen is rarely one job. There's demolition, cabinetry, countertops, flooring, a backsplash, sometimes plumbing and electrical. When those are five separate companies, every handoff is a date that can slip, and the homeowner ends up being the unwilling project manager. We handle kitchens, bathrooms, countertops, cabinet refacing, vanities, backsplashes, and flooring under one roof, which removes most of those handoffs. One schedule, one point of contact, one company accountable when something needs sorting out. We are fully licensed and insured for residential and commercial projects alike. None of that makes a remodel effortless. Walls still surprise people and deliveries still run late. It does mean nobody is standing in your kitchen explaining that the delay belongs to a different contractor. Fewer companies also means fewer people walking through your house, which matters more than people expect when the work runs for several weeks. If you're early in planning and want to see the range of what we take on, our homepage is a great place to start, then work from there. Serving Frederick and the surrounding Maryland communities.
Oct 5, 2026

From the owner
We were featured in an article on the Bob Vila website about cabinetry and we wanted to share it with you. “Shaker cabinets have by far been the most popular style for many years previously, and moving forward they will remain a strong choice,” says Fran Isaacson, CKBR, of Skippack, Pennsylvania-based Inspiration Kitchen and Bath, LLC. With its clean lines, flat-paneled fronts, and wide-framed doors, today’s Shaker-style kitchen cabinets remain true to the honest simplicity of its 18th-century Shaker origins. The plain design is also easier to maintain and wipe clean than more ornate styles. Called a “5-piece” for its five components (front panel, rails, and stiles) and painted in neutral colors like cream or stained in wood tones, Shaker-style kitchen cabinets fit well with many home styles, from traditional to modern farmhouse. When painted in bolder hues, they can even complement a modern home. Among all of the types of cabinets, this may be one of the easier styles for an experienced DIYer to attempt. We recommend trying to recreate this kitchen cabinet door style at least once before trying to undertake an entire kitchen upgrade. Click the "learn more" button to read the entire article.

Every fall, I hear some version of the same thing: “We’re thinking about renovating our kitchen next year.” And usually, “next year” means spring. From the owner
Casino and hospitality lighting changes how a pattern reads more than people expect. Low, warm lighting flattens color saturation, so a pattern that looked rich under daylight can read muddy once the overhead lights dim down. We always ask to see the room under its actual lighting before finalizing a selection, not just a swatch under a desk lamp. Metallic accents hold up better than matte finishes in low light, catching just enough shine to stay visible. Repeat patterns get chosen with sightlines in mind, since guests often view a wall from an angle, not straight on. Reno Wallpaper Installer accounts for lighting conditions on commercial jobs like that, alongside regular home work. Picking a pattern for a dim lounge or hallway? Test it under the actual lighting before committing.

From the owner
New kitchen cabinets deserve an installation that gets the details right. In Northern Virginia, professional cabinet installation typically costs $75–$175 per linear foot for labour. For a 20-linear-foot kitchen, that’s approximately $1,500–$3,500, separate from the cabinets themselves. But good installation involves more than hanging boxes on a wall. Uneven floors and out-of-square corners call for careful levelling, shimming and fitting. Proper fasteners, neatly scribed filler strips and adjusted hinges help your cabinets look right and work smoothly. What should a professional installation include? • Checking the cabinet delivery against your order • Locating studs and establishing a level line • Securing and levelling every cabinet • Fitting filler strips and specified trim • Adjusting doors and drawers for consistent gaps • Cleaning up the work area Most installs take two to four days once cabinets are on site. A working kitchen takes longer: countertops must be templated after the cabinets are installed and levelled, followed by fabrication. At Modern Kitchen & Bath, we supply and install kitchen cabinetry across Sterling and Northern Virginia, with an on-site measurement before quoting. Planning your project? Read our guide to costs, timelines and what to check before signing off: Contact us for a free estimate. Prices are planning ranges; your quote depends on layout and scope.

Before you hire a Cypress contractor, look closely at the quote. A real estimate is a roadmap, not a guess. Rock Creek Contracting is an engineer-led general contractor serving NW Houston, and owner Philip Blue (B.S. Civil Engineering) knows a vague lump sum is a red flag. A reliable quote shows a line item per trade, realistic allowances, written exclusions, and payments tied to finished milestones. Two Texas protections worth knowing: on a homestead, both spouses should sign before work begins to protect the contract, and holding back 10 percent retainage helps protect you if subcontractors are not paid. Read our complete guide before you sign.

From the owner
In Bothell, a deck spends much of the year wet, so the materials you choose affect how well it holds up. Here is how the rain should shape those decisions. Decking boards come first. Pressure-treated lumber and cedar resist rot better than untreated wood, but both need regular sealing and cleaning to keep moisture and moss in check. Composite and PVC decking resist rot and need less upkeep, which is a real advantage here, though some products can get slippery when wet and show mildew in shaded spots. Framing and fasteners matter as much as the surface. The structure underneath is exposed to the same moisture, so rot-resistant lumber, proper spacing, and corrosion-resistant screws and hardware help prevent early failure. Drainage and airflow protect everything. Gaps between boards, slope for runoff, and ventilation underneath let water escape instead of sitting. Flashing where the deck meets the house keeps water out of the wall. Surface safety deserves a thought. Textured or grooved boards improve traction on wet days, and moss and algae need regular cleaning. Finally, think about upkeep. The cheapest material may cost more over time if it needs frequent repair. Call us today to plan your deck remodel in Bothell.

Bathroom Remodeling That Makes the Whole Room Work Better What should a bathroom do besides look good? It should make the morning routine easier, give you enough room to move, and keep the main features from competing for space. With bathroom remodeling, we look at how each part of the room works together, including: • Shower size and entry space • Tub placement and surrounding clearance • Vanity storage and countertop room • Tile choices for floors and shower walls • Lighting around the vanity and bathing areas • Simple storage details such as built-in shower niches The layout matters just as much as the individual finishes. A large tile shower can provide comfortable room for daily use, while a separate tub creates another option without crowding the space. Vanity placement, walking paths, fixtures, and storage all need to make sense together. We plan these details around how the bathroom will actually be used, not just how it looks on a drawing. The result should feel organized, comfortable, and practical every time you walk in.

From the owner
🛁 Project Spotlight: Wallingford Tub-to-Shower Conversion 🛁 We recently completed a bathroom transformation for the Pascale family in Wallingford, turning a challenging layout into a modern oasis. The Challenge: The home’s bathroom featured an old, high-sided bathtub that was difficult to navigate. Paired with a dark shower curtain, the space felt cramped and lacked accessibility. The family needed a safe, functional, and visually appealing environment. The Solution: Our team at Bath Planet of CT removed the old tub and constructed a highly accessible walk-in shower. We installed floor-to-ceiling Calcutta Marble wall surrounds, adding an elegant white finish with beautiful grey veins. This brightened the room while providing a non-porous, easy-to-clean surface. To maximize safety, we incorporated a low-barrier shower pan for effortless entry. The old curtain was replaced with premium, smooth-gliding glass doors, instantly making the room feel larger. Finally, we added built-in corner shelving for organization, perfectly complemented by sparkling chrome hardware and a modern showerhead. The Outcome: What used to be a cramped hurdle is now a bright, expansive, and resort-worthy retreat. The Pascale family now enjoys a safe, beautiful bathroom that balances style and accessibility. Read the full case study on our website to see the amazing before and after photos! ✨

Case Study Summary: The Hiraldo Family’s Meriden Bathroom Makeover We Improve For You recently completed a bathroom transformation for the Hiraldo family in Meriden, Connecticut, converting a dated, high-threshold bathtub into a sleek, accessible walk-in shower. The original space was cramped and dark, featuring an old-fashioned bathtub with a high wall that made entry difficult and hazardous. The beige, grout-heavy tiles were difficult to clean and absorbed light, making the room feel enclosed. To address these challenges, the team updated the bathroom into a modern, accessible oasis. The old tub was removed and replaced with a low-barrier walk-in shower base, providing safe and effortless entry. Floor-to-ceiling Calcutta Marble wall surrounds were installed, offering an elegant, low-maintenance solution that eliminates the porous grout lines of traditional tile. To maximize light and give the space an open feel, clear glass sliding doors replaced the old shower curtain, visually doubling the size of the room. The update was finished with polished chrome fixtures and integrated corner shelving for convenient storage. The result is a bright, open, and practical space that provides the Hiraldo family with greater confidence, accessibility, and peace of mind in their home. Learn more about this Meriden bathroom makeover by visiting our latest case study.

From the owner
Drafty doors and windows in Michigan homes, and why they show up every fall - The first cold morning of October tells you a lot about your house. You notice the chill by the front door, the curtain that moves on its own and the bedroom that never quite warms up. Drafty doors and windows are the most common comfort complaint we hear from Southeast Michigan homeowners, and most of them can be fixed with carpentry rather than a replacement quote. Our draft sealing service exists because the fix is usually smaller than people fear. This guide walks through every place cold air gets past a door or a window, what you can check yourself on a Saturday and what calls for a trained set of hands. It covers entry doors, storm doors, patio doors, double-hung sashes, sills, trim and the caulk lines that hold it all together. When a section points to a job our Wright’s Repairs division handles, we link to it so you can see exactly what the visit includes. We are a design-build firm based in Ypsilanti, and over the years our crews have worked in older plaster-wall homes in Ann Arbor, postwar ranches in Westland and newer colonials in Canton. The draft problems look different in each, but the causes repeat. Worn seals, doors that moved out of square, sills that rotted from the bottom and caulk that gave up years ago account for nearly everything we find on a winterizing visit for Michigan homes. How Michigan housing stock shapes the problem...
